stories.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Mitsubishi Electric industrial software suites, including GENESIS and ICONICS, allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, bypass authentication, or trigger denial-of-service conditions. These flaws impact various versions, potentially leading to unauthorized data manipulation or system destruction.
stories.why: These flaws affect critical industrial control systems, posing significant risks to operational technology environments through potential remote code execution and authentication bypass.
stories.action: Review CISA advisory and apply available patches for affected Mitsubishi Electric software versions immediately.

stories.title: Apple Backports Fix for Exploited CoreGraphics Flaw to Older iPhones and iPads
PHP Issues Second Windows Security Update in Five Days to Fix Brotli Code Execution Flaw
stories.abstract: A critical memory corruption vulnerability in the Brotli compression library, CVE-2026-111497, allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via malformed compressed data. The flaw affects numerous platforms, including PHP Windows packages, Node.js, .NET, and various Python libraries that process Brotli-encoded traffic.
stories.why: This widespread vulnerability enables remote code execution in common web runtimes and proxies, posing a significant risk to server-side infrastructure.
stories.action: Update PHP, Node.js, and all Brotli-dependent libraries to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft releases emergency .NET security fixes for Google Brotli bug
CISA confirms PHP2Shell under attack as researchers clock successful exploits
stories.abstract: CISA has officially added two critical PHP vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Security researchers have confirmed that threat actors are actively leveraging these flaws to gain remote shell access on vulnerable systems.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical PHP vulnerabilities poses a significant risk of remote code execution and full server compromise.
stories.action: Patch all PHP instances to the latest secure versions immediately.

stories.title: CISA confirms PHP2Shell vulnerabilities now exploited in attacks
stories.abstract: CISA has officially added the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The agency confirmed that these flaws are currently being leveraged in active cyberattacks and has mandated that federal civilian agencies apply necessary patches by this Thursday.
stories.why: Active exploitation of web-based vulnerabilities poses a significant risk of unauthorized remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Patch all systems affected by PHP2Shell immediately.

stories.title: iOS, macOS 27.2 Patch 286 Bugs; Fix for Exploited Flaw Backported to iOS 18
stories.abstract: Apple released updates for iOS and macOS addressing 286 security vulnerabilities. The company also backported a fix for a previously exploited CoreGraphics zero-day to ensure protection for users on older versions of iOS 18.
stories.why: Massive vulnerability counts indicate significant underlying code instability, and backporting confirms the active exploitation of critical flaws in the graphics stack.
stories.action: Update all Apple devices to the latest available software versions immediately.

stories.title: University of Copenhagen data breach exposes data of 525,000 people
Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers
stories.abstract: Tailscale is addressing multiple vulnerabilities, including a critical flaw in its SSH implementation. If port forwarding is enabled, an attacker who compromises one device on the network can leverage these weaknesses to escalate privileges to root on other reachable servers.
stories.why: This flaw allows lateral movement and privilege escalation within a Tailscale mesh, undermining the security assumptions of zero-trust network access.
stories.action: Update Tailscale clients to the latest version and disable SSH port forwarding until patched.

stories.title: EPICS Base
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in EPICS Base versions 7.0.10 and earlier, including integer overflows and type confusion flaws, could allow remote attackers to trigger denial-of-service, corrupt memory, leak sensitive data, or achieve arbitrary code execution within industrial control environments.
stories.why: These flaws pose severe risks to critical infrastructure systems relying on EPICS Base for distributed control and data acquisition.
stories.action: Update EPICS Base to a version beyond 7.0.10.

stories.title: Microsoft releases out-of-band Windows fixes with certificate updates
stories.abstract: Microsoft issued out-of-band updates for Windows to revoke trust in specific eMudhra certificates. This measure addresses compromised certificate authority keys, ensuring that systems no longer rely on potentially malicious or insecure digital credentials for authentication and secure communications.
stories.why: Compromised CA keys allow attackers to issue fraudulent certificates, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks and the bypass of code-signing security controls.
stories.action: Install the latest out-of-band Windows updates immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
stories.abstract: Nearly 1,000 e-commerce sites, primarily utilizing Magento, have been compromised by a persistent threat actor. The attackers are injecting obfuscated JavaScript loaders directly into CMS blocks to evade automated security scanners and harvest sensitive customer data during the checkout process.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting e-commerce platforms directly expose customer payment information and undermine the integrity of online transaction environments.
stories.action: Audit Magento CMS blocks for unauthorized scripts and implement strict content security policies.

stories.title: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Critical Flaws in Collabora Online and Arista VeloCloud
Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in the Microsoft Authenticator app for Android allowed unauthorized applications to impersonate trusted services like Teams. This flaw enabled attackers to intercept and steal authentication tokens from enterprise user accounts without requiring any specific permissions on the victim's device.
stories.why: This bypasses multi-factor authentication protections, potentially granting attackers full access to sensitive corporate resources and cloud environments.
stories.action: Update Microsoft Authenticator for Android to version 6.2606.4246 or later.

stories.title: In-the-Wild Attack Abuses AI Agents' Trust in Markdown
stories.abstract: Researchers identified a novel prompt injection method targeting AI coding assistants. By manipulating local Markdown files, attackers can trick agents into executing unauthorized commands, effectively turning passive documentation into a vector for malicious system-level actions.
stories.why: This highlights a critical supply chain risk where AI agents blindly trust local configuration or instruction files, leading to potential remote code execution.

stories.title: [Control systems] Hitachi security advisory (AV26-1091)
stories.abstract: Hitachi has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting several versions of its HiRDB server software and various JP1 management tools. Additionally, the TRO600 series firmware requires updates to address security flaws identified in versions prior to 9.2.2.1.
stories.why: Unpatched industrial and management software can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical infrastructure and enterprise job scheduling systems.
stories.action: Review Hitachi security advisory AV26-1091 and apply available patches for affected HiRDB, JP1, and TRO600 products.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Moxa security advisory (AV26-1089)
stories.abstract: Moxa has disclosed three vulnerabilities affecting the Remote Connect Suite (MRC Client) version 4.2.0 and earlier, as well as all firmware versions of the OnCell G3150A-LTE series. Users should review the manufacturer's advisory for remediation details.
stories.why: These flaws impact industrial remote access and cellular gateway hardware, potentially allowing unauthorized control or access to critical operational technology environments.
stories.action: Review the official Moxa security advisory and apply available firmware or software updates.

stories.title: [Control systems] Johnson Controls security advisory (AV26-1090)
PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Risk Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
'Aokigahara' Stealer Targets 'Developer Keyrings' & AI Assistants
stories.abstract: A new information-stealing malware dubbed Aokigahara is actively targeting developer environments. The threat focuses on harvesting credentials from local keyrings and intercepting active AI assistant sessions, potentially exposing proprietary business data and internal infrastructure from a single infected machine.
stories.why: It signals a shift in malware tactics toward compromising AI-integrated workflows and developer secrets, increasing the impact of endpoint breaches.

stories.title: Hackers repeatedly breached suppliers holding UK police data, watchdog finds
stories.abstract: A UK government watchdog report revealed that police sensitive information was compromised multiple times over the last ten years due to security failures at third-party IT service providers.
stories.why: It highlights systemic supply chain vulnerabilities and the critical need for rigorous third-party risk management and oversight within law enforcement infrastructure.

stories.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
stories.abstract: Researchers discovered a vulnerability in OpenAI's conversation compaction feature that allowed unauthorized access to hidden AI reasoning traces. By manipulating the compression process, attackers could extract internal model thought processes that are typically encrypted and inaccessible to end users.
stories.why: Exposing internal reasoning chains could facilitate model inversion attacks, intellectual property theft, or the bypass of safety guardrails embedded in reasoning models.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Teams External Chat to Breach Organizations in Under 15 Minutes
stories.abstract: Threat actors are weaponizing Microsoft Teams' external chat feature to conduct rapid social engineering campaigns. By bypassing internal communication restrictions, attackers establish trust with employees to deploy ransomware and other malicious payloads within minutes of initial contact.
stories.why: External communication channels often bypass traditional security perimeters, providing a direct vector for social engineering and credential harvesting against internal staff.
stories.action: Restrict external Teams communication to verified domains and implement strict sender identity verification policies.

stories.title: From industry concern to practical action: the value of working with regulators
stories.abstract: The NCSC and the Financial Conduct Authority have established a collaborative framework for financial institutions to exchange threat intelligence. This initiative aims to streamline security information sharing while ensuring compliance with market integrity regulations and data protection standards.
stories.why: Standardized reporting channels reduce friction between regulatory compliance and incident response, improving the speed of collective defense within the financial sector.

stories.title: University of New Mexico hospital diverts ambulances after cyberattack
DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident"
stories.abstract: DreamHost has mandated password resets for email and FTP/SFTP accounts following a security incident that disrupted their File Manager interface. The company is currently investigating the scope of the unauthorized access and system impact.
stories.why: Forced credential resets suggest a potential compromise of authentication data or unauthorized access to administrative interfaces.
stories.action: Reset your DreamHost email and FTP passwords immediately and enable multi-factor authentication.

stories.title: Day 2 of canceled classes at University of New Mexico after Health Sciences Center cyberattack
Energy giant ENGIE discloses data breach affecting customers
stories.abstract: French utility provider ENGIE confirmed a data breach involving a third-party marketing platform. Unauthorized actors accessed and exfiltrated customer information stored within the system used by the company's business partners.
stories.why: Third-party vendor access remains a critical supply chain risk, often serving as a primary entry point for unauthorized data exfiltration.

stories.title: Cyber Incident Forces UNM Health to Cancel Surgeries, Divert Ambulances
IBM security advisory (AV26-1082)
Attackers Use Microsoft Teams IT Support Scams to Deploy Malware and Ransomware
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting Microsoft Teams' external chat functionality to impersonate IT support staff. By leveraging disposable tenant accounts, attackers deceive users into installing malicious software, facilitating ransomware deployment and unauthorized system access through persistent social engineering tactics.
stories.why: This highlights a significant risk in collaboration platforms where external communication features bypass traditional internal security perimeters.
stories.action: Restrict external access in Microsoft Teams to verified domains and educate users on IT support verification.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Tuesday, October 27th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10152, (Tue, Oct 27th)
AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
stories.abstract: Generative AI tools are lowering the barrier for creating highly convincing, brand-impersonating phishing sites. These sophisticated portals are increasingly capable of bypassing standard defenses by capturing multi-factor authentication tokens and hijacking active user sessions in real-time.
stories.why: Automated, high-fidelity phishing significantly increases the success rate of account takeovers, rendering traditional credential-based security controls less effective.

stories.title: Maritime Coalition Launches Free Vulnerability Database for Ship and Port Systems
stories.abstract: A new industry coalition has introduced the Blue Initiative, a centralized database cataloging approximately 30,000 IT and OT vulnerabilities. The repository specifically highlights 37 flaws affecting maritime-sector hardware and software to help secure global shipping and port infrastructure.
stories.why: It provides specialized threat intelligence for critical maritime infrastructure, which often lacks dedicated security oversight and faces unique operational technology risks.

stories.title: Apple Patches for October 2026, (Mon, Oct 26th)
Red Hat security advisory (AV26-1084)
Malicious apps prey on Russians’ anxiety about fuel prices, drone strikes
stories.abstract: Threat actors are distributing infostealer malware disguised as utility applications in Russia. These malicious tools masquerade as trackers for regional drone activity, local police movements, and fluctuating fuel costs to compromise user devices.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how attackers weaponize localized geopolitical anxiety and real-time information needs to facilitate credential theft and system compromise.

stories.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
stories.abstract: South Korean authorities have apprehended seven individuals accused of compromising over 90 organizations. The group allegedly utilized a specialized penetration testing framework known as ARTEX AI to exfiltrate more than 8.2 million sensitive records from various domestic entities.
stories.why: This incident highlights the growing risk of offensive security tools being weaponized by threat actors to automate large-scale data theft.

stories.title: Japanese virtual desktop cloud hacked so hard it asks to be banned
Lazarus Abuses South Korean Security Software to Deploy Malware Using Post-Quantum Encryption
stories.abstract: The Lazarus Group is conducting a targeted espionage campaign against South Korean firms in the construction and technology sectors. The operation, identified as FlashHole, utilizes compromised security software to distribute malware protected by post-quantum encryption methods to evade detection.
stories.why: The use of post-quantum encryption in malware signals an evolution in threat actor capabilities to bypass traditional traffic inspection and analysis tools.

stories.title: Microsoft 365 Token-Replay Attacks Compromise 97 Accounts at 79 Organizations
stories.abstract: Attackers are conducting adversary-in-the-middle campaigns to hijack Microsoft 365 session tokens. By intercepting authentication flows, threat actors successfully compromised nearly 100 accounts across dozens of organizations, facilitating business email compromise and unauthorized access to corporate environments.
stories.why: Session token theft bypasses traditional multi-factor authentication, rendering standard login protections ineffective against sophisticated phishing and relay attacks.
stories.action: Implement conditional access policies and enforce phishing-resistant authentication methods like FIDO2 security keys.

stories.title: CISA warns of PHP bug exploitation attempts, gives federal agencies days to patch
US government says hackers are now exploiting critical PHP web bugs
stories.abstract: CISA has issued an alert confirming that threat actors are actively exploiting critical vulnerabilities within PHP. Given that this language powers a vast majority of web applications, the potential for widespread compromise of server-side infrastructure is significant.
stories.why: PHP vulnerabilities often lead to remote code execution, granting attackers full control over web servers and the data they host.
stories.action: Audit PHP-based applications and ensure all environments are running the latest patched versions.

stories.title: Attackers Hijack Dahua IP Cameras in Ukraine Using P2P Access and Auth Weaknesses
Japan internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data
Warp discloses breach exposing AI agent logs, user telemetry data
stories.abstract: Terminal developer Warp suffered a data breach after a third-party vendor was compromised. The incident exposed sensitive user telemetry and logs generated by the company's AI-powered development agents, potentially revealing internal workflows or code-related context to unauthorized parties.
stories.why: Exposed agent logs may contain proprietary code snippets, API keys, or sensitive environment details processed by AI development tools.

stories.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
The Huntress Tragic Quadrant: Ranking Threats Hitting Businesses Hardest
Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
stories.abstract: Keystone is decommissioning nearly 19,000 hardware wallets after a website breach exposed the private key used for device authenticity verification. This compromise allows attackers to manufacture counterfeit hardware that successfully bypasses the company's official validation checks, posing a significant risk to user assets.
stories.why: Supply chain integrity is compromised; attackers can now produce fraudulent hardware that appears legitimate to the manufacturer's verification systems.
stories.action: Verify your device status via Keystone's official support channels and monitor for replacement instructions.

stories.title: UK Politician Jess Asato Got Deepfaked. Now She’s Taking xAI to Court
stories.abstract: UK Member of Parliament Jess Asato is initiating legal action against xAI after the company's Grok AI tool generated non-consensual deepfake imagery of her. This incident highlights the growing risks of generative AI platforms being weaponized to harass public figures.
stories.why: It underscores the legal and reputational risks organizations face when their generative models are exploited to create harmful, non-consensual content.

stories.title: Looking for a Language [Guest Diary], (Wed, Oct 21st)
stories.abstract: A guest contributor from the SANS BACS program explores the challenges of selecting an appropriate programming language for security-focused tasks, weighing factors like performance, library availability, and ease of implementation in defensive or offensive workflows.
stories.why: Choosing the right tool impacts the efficiency, maintainability, and security posture of custom automation and analysis scripts.

Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
Australia Gets Into Amadey Malware Backend, Cuts Off Access to 180,000 Infected Computers
Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
Between alerts: What Attackers Do in the Spaces Ordinary Detection Misses
uCreator Android Spyware Can Steal Telegram 2FA Passwords and Clone WeChat Accounts
GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
Bias in Qwen3-Coder Model
